steps.step: Meet to plan Yellow Belt training dates and delivery format
steps.rule: They try to set a six-week cadence and alternate between virtual and in person; the dates may cover a six-month period or the end of the year.

steps.step: Determine whether the session is open registration or department requested
steps.trigger: A Yellow Belt session is being planned
steps.rule: The process depends on whether it is an open-registration session or a department-requested session.

steps.step: For a department-requested session, meet with the sponsor and set up the agreement
steps.trigger: A department requests a Yellow Belt session
steps.rule: The agreement explains what each party is responsible for; the sponsor provides project and task numbers; internal and sponsor signatures are obtained.

steps.step: Submit the scheduled dates for class listing
steps.system: Services and support ticket; UC Learning
steps.rule: The dates are submitted through a services and support ticket so the classes can be listed in UC Learning.

steps.step: Add the dates to internal calendars and publish them
steps.trigger: The class dates are ready to communicate
steps.rule: The internal calendar is in Outlook, and the dates are posted on the website through the CMS.

steps.step: Request and track facilitator coverage
steps.rule: Upcoming dates and facilitator support are discussed in Tuesday or Friday team meetings.

steps.step: Prepare the virtual session access and course materials
steps.rule: A calendar invite includes Zoom; the same open Zoom link is typically used; a PowerPoint version is prepared.

steps.step: Discover and compare training options
steps.trigger: Looking for professional development and Lean Six Sigma training

steps.step: Ask which program fits
steps.trigger: The attendee is unsure which training to apply for
steps.who: Attendee; DES, Transformational Healthcare Team, and OSI staff
steps.rule: The best fit is determined based on the person’s situation and, as Angela described, staff affiliation.
steps.whatGoesWrong: The attendee said, “I was confused about that” and was “not being sure which one I was supposed to apply for.”

steps.step: Direct the attendee to a program and provide the UC Learning link
steps.rule: Angela directs staff to Transformational Healthcare Team or OSI depending on whether they are health system or campus staff; the attendee was told OSI was the best fit.

steps.step: Register for the class
steps.trigger: The attendee receives the UC Learning link
steps.rule: The attendee uses an AD login and acknowledges the platform checkbox before registering.
steps.whatGoesWrong: The attendee got “like, an error” until checking “some acknowledgement, like a checkbox” in UC Learning.

steps.step: Pull the roster and prepare participant tracking
steps.system: UC Learning; internal attendance Excel tracker
steps.rule: For open registration, Tony pulls the attendee list from UC Learning and places it on an internal tracker; for a department session, the sponsor provides the roster.

steps.step: Create the participant Teams environment and add attendees
steps.rule: Tony duplicates a channel from a previous iteration, updates the templates, and adds virtual attendees one by one.
steps.whatGoesWrong: Tony said, “I have to add them manually, because there's not a batch way to add them.”

steps.step: Send class reminders and update the roster
steps.trigger: The session is approaching and participant information changes
steps.rule: A reminder template is sent; about a day before the session, late cancellations and late adds are reviewed and the roster is changed as needed.
steps.whatGoesWrong: Late cancellations and late adds require roster changes.

steps.step: Attend the virtual training and complete the course activities
steps.rule: The training uses Zoom sessions, a day-one Kahoot quiz, and a day-two Lucidchart future-state mapping activity; department-requested sessions may use Google or Miro instead.

steps.step: Receive homework instructions and submit assignments
steps.trigger: Day one of the session ends
steps.rule: Tony sends a homework reminder with attachments; participants submit assignments over the next day or two.

steps.step: Review homework and provide feedback
steps.rule: Tony gives feedback on submissions and writes notes about common themes.

steps.step: Create certificates after attendance is known
steps.trigger: The end of day one, when attendance is known
steps.rule: Tony waits until the end of day one because people can drop or be added late.

steps.step: Send post-class information and survey
steps.rule: Participants receive thanks, a survey link, information about certificates in the Teams folder, and information about continued Teams access.

steps.step: Record attendance and update OSI participant records
steps.rule: Tony marks attendees present and non-attendees absent, then updates a raw headcount sheet and a sheet with participant names, emails, and attendance dates.

steps.step: Process the department recharge when applicable
steps.rule: There are currently no fees for the described open-registration sessions; for a department-requested session, the department is recharged rather than individuals.

steps.step: Receive the certificate and consider next steps
steps.trigger: The class ends and the certificate is available
steps.whatGoesWrong: The attendee said, “I feel a little bit overwhelmed. A little unsure of where to go next. Because it was a lot of information kind of overload.”
